findings.rationale: Update norm is inflated against size-matched peers from round 1 onward (median norm ratio 3.9, z about +7 after size adjustment) while mean cosine to the median update is low (0.32). Per-round norm ratios stay between 2.3 and 5.0 in every round, and cosines are mostly near 0 to 0.5. This pattern fits large random noise added to uploads rather than honest training. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.833, CITL 0.006), so the local data looks fine. Confidence is moderate because the cosine is noisy at this epsilon.

Update norm is about 4x the median (size-adjusted z about +6), with a low mean cosine (0.29). Norm ratios are highest early (6.8 in round 1) and fall later, but stay well above peers. Cosines are noisy and around zero in later rounds, which fits random noise rather than a consistent sign-flip. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.849, CITL -0.0006). Confidence is moderate.

Update norm is inflated across the run (median norm ratio 3.6, z about +6). Cosine to the median update is positive in rounds 1 to 13 and then turns negative from round 14 (-0.10, -0.58, -0.27, -0.02, -0.29, -0.10, -0.32 across rounds 14 to 20). A sustained reversal of direction is what a sign-flipped or scaled poisoned upload would produce, not random noise. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.810, CITL -0.011), so the local data looks fine. Confidence is moderate.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients on updates, performance, drift, features and subgroups, then spent the remaining budget confirming the leads. Three clients (UT, NY, FL) have update norms about 3.6–4.1x size-matched peers, persistently across rounds, with low cosine to the median update. I report UT and NY as explanation_instability (noise-like uploads from round 1, moderate confidence). FL shows a sustained negative cosine from round 14, which I read as poisoning from round 14 (moderate confidence). Local AUC, CITL and prevalence are normal for all three, so their data looks fine. Other leads did not hold up: NC's GenHlth p99 anomaly disappeared on a narrower re-check, ND's HighChol spread is not supported by its percentiles, and the WV Income-6 and GU Sex O/E outliers came from small clients without a second confirming signal. No client showed label-noise, prevalence-shift or drift flags. Confidence on the fault-type split for the three update clients is moderate, because the cosine estimates are noisy at the epsilon I could afford.
